# Badge

A short label for a status or category, with an icon and a border on status tones.

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@kafka-ds/react'
```

## When to use it

- To tell the state of something: "Inscripciones abiertas", "Agotado", "Miembros".

## When not to

- As a button: a badge is not interactive. Use Chip.
- For long text: keep it to two or three words.
- Colour as the only difference: status tones also carry an icon.

## Examples

### Tones

Status tones carry an icon and a border, so they work without colour. Neutral and brand are for categories.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
  <Badge>Taller</Badge>
  <Badge tone="brand" Icon={IconCrown}>Miembros</Badge>
  <Badge tone="info">Próximamente</Badge>
  <Badge tone="success">Inscripciones abiertas</Badge>
  <Badge tone="warning">Últimos cupos</Badge>
  <Badge tone="danger">Agotado</Badge>
</div>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tone` | `BadgeTone` | `'neutral'` | The meaning. Status tones carry an icon so colour is never the only signal. |
| `Icon` | `IconType \| null` |  | Replaces the tone's icon. Use `null` to remove it. |
| …rest | `HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>` | | Everything else is passed to the underlying element. |

## Accessibility

- **Not by colour alone:** info, success, warning and danger each have an icon and a 1 px border in the status colour (3:1 against the page).
- **Contrast:** text is 4.5:1 or better on its tint, in both modes.
- The icon is decorative; the text carries the meaning.

## Content

- Two or three words, no full stop.
